title: anywaye health probe contract
description: The healthz/readyz split, as a machine-checkable shape. `healthz` is UNCONDITIONAL liveness — 'the process is up' — and must consult nothing, because a liveness check that touches a dependency turns a database outage into a restart loop, and restarting every container that depends on a database does not restore the database. `readyz` is readiness and MUST actually check its dependencies, because without it a load balancer cheerfully routes traffic into a service whose database is gone. darkroom is the pattern to standardise on: `/healthz` never touches a dependency, `/readyz` really runs `select 1`, and both are exempt from authentication by an explicit path allow-list rather than by route ordering — a `/healthz` behind the auth middleware returns 401, every instance is marked unhealthy, and the deployment rolls back with no indication why. `minItems: 1` on `readyz.checks` is the rule this schema exists to enforce: a `readyz` that checks nothing is the failure mode, and it is invisible because the endpoint returns 200 and looks perfect in every dashboard. See docs/observability.md.

service.description: The service this declaration describes, equal to `name` in its anywaye.yml.

healthz.description: Liveness. Unconditional by construction: `checks` is `maxItems: 0`, so a declaration that gives liveness a dependency check cannot validate.

readyz.description: Readiness. `minItems: 1` on `checks`, so a service with a `readyz` that checks nothing fails the schema rather than shipping.

livenessProbe.description: Liveness: 'the process is up', and nothing else. The dependency list is constrained to be EMPTY rather than merely documented as empty, so a `healthz` that starts consulting the database is a schema failure. The reasoning is the restart loop: a liveness probe that fails on a dependency tells the orchestrator to restart a process that is fine, which turns a database outage into a fleet-wide crash loop and destroys the evidence you need to diagnose it.

path.description: The literal path. Pinned, so a self-hoster's orchestrator, their dashboard and their runbook all address the same URL in every one of the six services.

auth.description: Exempt from authentication, by an explicit path allow-list rather than by route order. This is the field that goes wrong silently: a probe behind the auth middleware returns 401, an orchestrator marks every instance unhealthy, and the rollback message says nothing about authentication. darkroom's README records the test that caught it — axum's `Router::layer` applies to every route the router holds, so registering the probes 'before' the auth layer does not exempt them.

checks.description: Always empty. `maxItems: 0` is the whole rule: liveness consults nothing, so there is nothing to declare. A body is `{"status": "ok"}` and nothing else — no version, no timestamp, no host-specific data, because a probe whose body varies is a probe whose diff fills a support ticket.

readinessProbe.description: Readiness: 'should traffic come here'. The dependency list is REQUIRED and NON-EMPTY, which is the rule that has teeth — an empty `checks` array is the failure the whole schema exists to prevent, and it passes every eyeball test because the endpoint returns 200.

path.description: The literal path, pinned for the same reason as `/healthz`.

auth.description: Exempt from authentication, for the same reason and by the same explicit path allow-list. A `readyz` behind the auth middleware is the same incident as a `healthz` behind it: 401, every instance unhealthy, a rollback that says nothing about why.

statusCode.description: 200 when every required check passes, 503 otherwise. Note that readiness answers 503 rather than a non-listening error, because some orchestrators read any non-2xx as 'not listening' and would restart a container that is running perfectly well.

checks.description: The dependencies readiness actually consults. `minItems: 1` is a floor, not a hint: a service whose `readyz` checks nothing is reporting that it can serve traffic when it cannot, and the cost is discovered by a customer rather than by a test.

items.description: One dependency. `dependency` is required and is a name rather than a boolean, so a check that checks nothing cannot be declared — a boolean invites `true` for a check nobody wrote.

name.description: The slot name in the response's `checks` map, e.g. `db`, `provider_registry`.

dependency.description: What is actually consulted: `postgresql`, `redis`, `the provider registry`, `the outbox table`. A string, because 'the thing readiness would break without' is the useful half of the declaration and a boolean throws it away.

timeoutMs.description: Per-check timeout. Bounded at 10 seconds, because a readiness probe that can take longer than the orchestrator's own probe interval is a probe whose answer arrives after the decision it was meant to inform.

required.description: false marks a check whose failure degrades rather than removes the instance from the load balancer — the cost is real (a route that needs no database read can still be served) and it has to be written down, because an unstated degradation reads as an outage.
